- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–7 days.  
- If true price drops sharply after a peak, model often lags; adjust forecast downward by 1–4% in next 3–5 days if sentiment turns negative.  
- If model forecast mean is > true mean by >2%, and sentiment is neutral or mixed, apply mean reversion: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is > true by >10% in first 5 days, model is overconfident; cap forecast at 10% above true for next 3 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model often misreads trend; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to adjust forecast.
